name: jp2a
why: Turns JPGs into ASCII art, a familiar image-to-text transform, though its novelty has largely been absorbed by chafa-style tools.

brief.what_it_is: jp2a is a command-line tool that converts JPG images into ASCII art for display in a terminal. Per its release notes it also reads PNG and WebP, and it can output HTML or XHTML as well as plain text. Options in the release notes include truecolor and 256-color terminal output, edge shading (--edge-threshold=N.N), and centering the image in the terminal. The README itself did not load, so the command-line details here come only from the release notes.
brief.why_it_exists: The README did not load, so I have no author framing for why it exists. The brew description is simply "Convert JPG images to ASCII".

commands_seen.context: Option from the 1.2.0 release notes that enables edge shading when set to a desired threshold. This is a flag fragment seen in release notes, not a full command line.

brief.install_notes: Only the brew formula name and executable (jp2a) were given. The release notes mention a Docker image (fixed in 1.3.2 to include the missing libexif library), so a container route exists. I found no build-from-source steps, runtime requirements, or first-run configuration because the README did not load. The 1.3.2 notes say source builds are unaffected by that Docker fix.
brief.standout: It is an older image-to-ASCII tool with a long release history, and it handles image orientation through Exif metadata. The scout note says its novelty has largely been absorbed by chafa-style tools, so the entry should frame it as a classic rather than a new idea.
